text:
Montreal lost a game it arguably deserved to win, and the second period explains why. PIT scored four times in 14 minutes, including a power-play tip-in from Ben Kindel, and led 5-1 on chances that rated between 6 and 22 percent each. Jakub Dobes allowed 3.15 goals more than the shots he faced should have produced. Nick Suzuki's best look of the night, a 24 percent chance, was stopped by Arturs Silovs, and the deficit stood.

Then MTL took the third. They out-chanced PIT 1.34 to 0.49 in expected goals and had 69 shot attempts to PIT's 52 for the game. Cole Caufield cut it to 5-3 early in the period. With the net presumably empty late, Chris Kreider scored at 18:52 and Ivan Demidov tied it 24 seconds later at 19:16, both on even-strength goals set up by Suzuki, who finished with a goal and three assists. MTL had the edge in simulated replays, deserving the win 55 percent of the time to PIT's 45.

The overtime lasted 1:33. Tommy Novak, who had already scored in the second, took a pass from Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang and ended it with a wrist shot rated at 15 percent. Novak finished with two goals and an assist and was named first star. PIT's power play went 2 for 4 against MTL's 0 for 2, and that 0.86 to 0.06 expected-goals gap on the man advantage nearly decided the game on its own.
